title: Dividing-line reading of the computation: ES is a 'random covering' with log³ intensity, Crocker's problem a 'random covering' with log intensity
connection: In the residue model, ES's hit intensity grows like (log X)³ (families up to X), so failures become rarer than any power of X; p + 2^a + 2^b has intensity ≈ log n, giving failure probability ≈ n^{−c}, compatible with infinitely many structured failures.
why: Places ES and Crocker's problem on one axis (intensity growth) where ES is comfortably on the 'all n' side, provided independence holds; the open question is only correlation/structure.
